observed.probe: production catalog scenarios, phone-390 light EN canonical frame, Chromium; no scenario failures

onboarding-start/first-run.scenario: First empty visit. The hero with its headline, subtitle, Build, Track and chips, Privacy, and the device-local seen state; the bands below it are catalogued by the scrolled first-run states.

onboarding-start/first-run-proof.scenario: The landing scrolled to the proof band: seven steps over the real workout screen, with the pinned phone, lens and rail, and the persistent Build control.

onboarding-start/first-run-ways.scenario: The landing scrolled to the three ways to start, with the paste hand-off closed.

onboarding-start/first-run-track.scenario: The landing scrolled to the three engine outcomes and the strength-trend chart.

onboarding-start/first-run-data.scenario: The landing scrolled to the ink data band and its three rows.

onboarding-start/first-run-faq-open.scenario: The landing scrolled to the questions with the RIR answer open.

onboarding-start/first-run-close.scenario: The landing scrolled to the closing orange band; the persistent Build control has stepped aside.

onboarding-start/first-run-returning.scenario: A later visit to an empty device with nothing saved: the returning landing leads with a welcome back and the Build and Track actions, and condenses the page below.

onboarding-start/first-run-returning-res.scenario: A later visit with a half-finished Recommend setup saved: the lead action names the saved route and opens the chooser's resume card.

onboarding-start/hub.scenario: Create a program. Recommend is the sole primary path; Custom is its generated alternative; Browse stands alone; Bring or build is collapsed.

onboarding-start/hub-own-open.scenario: The Bring or build disclosure expanded with aria-expanded to reveal Build, paste, and Taurifer-file import paths.

onboarding-start/hub-existing.scenario: Opened from Settings while a program is active, so replacement consequences are in view.

onboarding-start/hub-help.scenario: The Not sure which one? helper expanded on the hub: two short questions that end in Continue with the suggested route, reaching all five jobs.

onboarding-recommend/desired-result.scenario: Route header, Cancel, progress 1 of 5, three desired-result choices.

onboarding-recommend/background.scenario: The carried goal with Change, then structured-program experience and recent six-week consistency.

onboarding-recommend/schedule.scenario: Days per week, session-minute ceiling, preferred rest.

onboarding-recommend/environment.scenario: Environment shortcuts with the capability correction disclosure closed.

onboarding-recommend/priorities.scenario: Primary priorities plus optional movement and exercise-avoidance controls.

onboarding-recommend/avoidance-pain.scenario: One avoided exercise with the pain reason selected and its safety copy.

onboarding-recommend/result.scenario: The program first: name, four facts, the week with its first day open, the answers it was built from as chips, why it fits, and the pinned activation.

onboarding-recommend/result-existing.scenario: The merged candidate surface while the current program remains untouched.

onboarding-recommend/replacement-confirm.scenario: The explicit archive-and-replace confirmation. History is not changed.

onboarding-recommend/activation-conflict.scenario: Another tab changed the active program. The newer program stays active.

onboarding-custom/desired-result.scenario: The custom route's own header and step count, not Recommend's.

onboarding-custom/background.scenario: Structured-program experience and recent consistency in the custom route.

onboarding-custom/schedule.scenario: Days per week, session ceiling and preferred rest in the custom route.

onboarding-custom/environment.scenario: Environment shortcuts in the custom route.

onboarding-custom/priorities.scenario: Each muscle has one accessible emphasis setting before exercise preferences.

onboarding-custom/exercise-preferences.scenario: One library search offers Include or Avoid, with separate selected lists.

onboarding-custom/result.scenario: The custom program first, with muscle emphasis and exercise preferences among the answer chips, and the pinned activation.

onboarding-browse/schedule.scenario: Days per week and session length, the only questions Browse asks.

onboarding-browse/environment.scenario: Environment shortcuts before the catalogue is filtered.

onboarding-browse/catalogue.scenario: Released, complete, tested programs with purpose, frequency and mismatches.

onboarding-browse/preview.scenario: The common review surface for a catalogue program.

onboarding-build/setup.scenario: The build_setup step: program name and day count before the editor opens.

onboarding-build/editor-empty.scenario: Real empty day containers, Add exercise, Save draft, activation disabled.

onboarding-build/editor-partial.scenario: One populated day and one incomplete day. Activation stays disabled.

onboarding-build/editor-ready.scenario: A complete manual draft with supported progression and activation enabled.

onboarding-import/source.scenario: The bounded supported-file and setup-source surface before any mutation.

onboarding-import/freeform-empty.scenario: The free-form door as it opens: an empty field, and the hand-off to ChatGPT or Claude still unavailable.

onboarding-import/freeform-filled.scenario: A pasted program with both app links live, the character counter, and the field the reply comes back into.

onboarding-import/freeform-stage2.scenario: Stage 2 with collapsed source summary, Edit button, ChatGPT and Claude buttons, and Preview prompt disclosure.

onboarding-import/freeform-stage3.scenario: Stage 3 with collapsed source summary, Import from clipboard, the "or paste" divider, reply textarea, Review CTA, Try another assistant, and Start over.

onboarding-import/freeform-gaps.scenario: Gap resolution screen with inputs for missing sets and reps, and the non-imported disclosure.

onboarding-import/freeform-gaps-invalid.scenario: Gap resolution screen after submitting empty inputs, highlighting invalid fields with .is-invalid and aria-invalid.

onboarding-import/freeform-unreadable.scenario: Unreadable reply recovery block with Copy repair prompt and Try another assistant actions.

onboarding-import/review.scenario: Reviewing candidate matches: a settled row with Change, candidate chips, an expanded disclosure, and unmatched escape hatches.

onboarding-import/preview.scenario: A mapped exercise with manual progression ownership and provenance.

onboarding-shared/gate.scenario: An incoming setup link adapts the landing around its safe program summary. Nothing persists until Start.

onboarding-shared/invalid.scenario: An invalid setup link explains that nothing was saved and keeps safe Build and Track actions available.

onboarding-shared/preview.scenario: The editable preview a shared payload lands in before explicit activation.

onboarding-recovery/resume.scenario: The resumable notice after reload: route, step, recency, Resume, Start over.

onboarding-recovery/rules-drift.scenario: A draft whose compiler rules are stale. Rebuild is required before activation.

onboarding-recovery/cancel-confirm.scenario: Cancel pressed mid-flow. A dialog over the current step asks whether to keep the draft or discard it; Escape or Continue setup returns to the step.

onboarding-recovery/restart-confirm.scenario: Start over pressed on a review. A dialog asks before the answers and the unused program are discarded; the active program does not change.

today/no-program.scenario: A fresh device after leaving setup, with no program or workout controls.

today/ready.scenario: The Direction D lifter before Day 1 starts: the prescription table reads recommendation() for every exercise, with the verdict tally above it.

today/mixed-strategies.scenario: The Direction D mixed day: anchor and back-off, rep goal, fixed effort, a manual slot in soft ink with no mark, a custom exercise and a lift with a set logged without RIR.

today/rest-bar.scenario: A logged set has started the inline rest countdown; the timer sheet remains closed after leaving Focus.

today/done.scenario: The Direction D lifter's finished Monday: totals, the record line, each lift's outcome and next target, View today's session as the primary control.

workout/focus-glossary.scenario: A definition is open after tapping a glossary term in Focus.

workout/stale-draft.scenario: A conflicting tab won while this tab retains a pending field value and offers Reload latest or Copy value.

workout/persist-retry.scenario: A field write was interrupted; the exact pending value remains visible beside Retry and Copy value actions.

workout/invalid-draft.scenario: An unreadable local draft remains untouched and offers a non-destructive copy action.

workout/rest-running.scenario: A logged set has started the rest: the clock on the rest-clock role, the orange drain bar and the next set's cue take the cue slot, and the rest controls take the shelf's pad row.

workout/rest-done.scenario: The rest has run out: the clock collapses to one line that counts the overrun up in soft ink, the cue returns and the field pads come back.

workout/why-this-weight.scenario: The recommendation inspector for a range lift: sentences first, each under a bold lead, the working behind See the working, the evidence footer.

workout/why-in-session.scenario: Opened after set 1 is logged: what the set showed (the observed capacity) before the prediction for the next set.

workout/why-rep-goal.scenario: Rep goal: the total, the effort gate and how the reps split.

workout/why-anchor.scenario: Anchor and back-off: the performed top set, the rule, and the percentage that sets the lighter sets.

workout/why-manual.scenario: Manual: one sentence; the program sets the load and the engine does not change it.

session/summary.scenario: The Direction D lifter's Day 1: maintained, improved and declined words, records in green, and each lift ending on its next target.

session/summary-maintained.scenario: A finished Day 2 whose Romanian deadlift is maintained, with its other lifts improved and a record.

session/summary-declined.scenario: A finished Day 3 that reports declined lifts in ink, without turning the result into a prescription.

session/summary-first.scenario: Every lift is a first exposure: the baseline sentence, no outcome words, and the next targets from the engine.

session/summary-mixed.scenario: The Direction D mixed day finished: anchor and back-off, rep goal, fixed effort, a manual lift and a custom exercise, with improved and maintained words, a lift without RIR and its records.

progress/overview-baseline.scenario: Sparse evidence remains neutral and contributes no Needs action items.

progress/overview-action.scenario: Sufficient evidence produces linked program-wide action items.

progress/strength-current-block.scenario: Current-block values, outcomes, and drill-in share one scope.

progress/strength-all-history.scenario: All-history scope explicitly includes archived observations.

progress/strength-comparison.scenario: Two compatible points show values, dates, absolute change, and percentage change.

progress/strength-sparse.scenario: Zero or one compatible point remains neutral baseline evidence.

progress/volume.scenario: The Volume sub-tab and its muscle rows.

progress/volume-block.scenario: Block-to-date volume uses elapsed weekly prescriptions.

progress/volume-drill-in.scenario: A primary muscle row expands to its scoped session evidence.

progress/prs-drill-in.scenario: A personal record expands to locale-formatted evidence detail.

progress/review-complete.scenario: A completed block exposes the evidence-valid structural routes.

progress/review-insufficient.scenario: A completed block with sparse evidence excludes performance-derived actions.

progress/schedule-diagnosis.scenario: The one-question choice between fewer days and shorter sessions.

progress/sibling-lower-frequency.scenario: A provenance-backed lower-frequency sibling diff before confirmation.

progress/sibling-shorter-session.scenario: A provenance-backed shorter-session sibling diff before confirmation.

progress/guided-repair.scenario: The exact current program is staged for explicit guided editing.

progress/volume-reduction-preview.scenario: The protected permanent-volume reduction diff before confirmation.

progress/recovery-ineligible.scenario: Recovery stays unavailable without sufficient qualifying pattern evidence.

progress/recovery-questions.scenario: Eligible pattern evidence still requires the explicit local readiness answer.

progress/recovery-preview.scenario: The policy-versioned week-one prescription diff before confirmation.

progress/recovery-active.scenario: The confirmed recovery overlay is visible during week one.

progress/recovery-reassessment.scenario: Canonical week two asks Better, About the same, or Worse.

history/edit-dirty.scenario: A session edit with an unsaved canonical change and its destructive actions still visible.

history/edit-invalid.scenario: An invalid set value is held at the field boundary with the editor's validation state visible.

history/delete-confirm.scenario: The explicit delete confirmation surface for one selected session.

history/conflict.scenario: A stale session edit refuses to overwrite a newer durable change and offers recovery actions.

library/list-selected.scenario: One movement is selected and the persistent add bar remains visible.

library/exercise-detail-glossary.scenario: A definition is open after tapping a term in movement detail.

program/no-program.scenario: A fresh device's Program tab, with setup as the only action.

program/overview.scenario: The current program and its days.

program/progression-editor.scenario: The installed program editor, with the first day open.

program/custom-exercise-saving.scenario: A new custom movement is saving; its actions stay unavailable until the durable write settles.

program/custom-exercise-deleting.scenario: A custom movement is deleting; the action names deletion and all competing actions stay unavailable until the durable write settles.

program/custom-exercise-archiving.scenario: A custom movement referenced by a performedMovementId-only history row is archiving; the action names archive and preserves its history identity.

program/custom-exercise-recovery.scenario: A partial archive stays visibly unresolved with recovery status, Retry recovery, and Reload actions.

program/share-one-blocker.scenario: The share sheet names one unresolved exercise and keeps copy/share unavailable.

program/share-repair-return.scenario: The custom repair path has been cancelled and returns directly to the blocked Share sheet.

program/share-ready.scenario: A valid setup link is ready for copy or system sharing.

settings/guides.scenario: The per-guide replay controls; replay changes presentation state only.

settings/guides-replay.scenario: A real contextual guide replayed from Settings and anchored to its live privacy action.

settings/privacy-disclosure.scenario: The cached ADR 0013 disclosure reached from Settings.

install/transfer-eligible.scenario: The pre-action transfer explanation and explicit consent.

install/transfer-ready.scenario: Successful creation followed by Safari installation instructions.

install/transfer-retryable.scenario: A definitive pre-create failure with retry and install-without-transfer actions.

install/transfer-claiming.scenario: The installed app is claiming its one-time transfer.

install/transfer-importing.scenario: The installed app is atomically importing the clone.

install/transfer-success.scenario: Verified local import and remote deletion are complete.

install/transfer-cleanup.scenario: Local import succeeded while verified remote deletion still needs retry.

install/transfer-terminal.scenario: The transfer is definitively unavailable and the installed app can continue safely.

install/transfer-destination.scenario: Existing installed-app data prevents replacement by a transfer.

install/transfer-interrupted.scenario: A recoverable installed import failure offers an explicit retry.

install/transfer-unknown.scenario: An indeterminate source outcome remains frozen until explicit divergence confirmation.

install/transfer-claimed-expired.scenario: Claimed-expired recovery remains frozen until explicit divergence confirmation.

workout/session.scenario: Session details and map through production controls.

workout/early-finish.scenario: Early finish confirmation through production controls.

today/draft-resume.scenario: Resume saved draft through production controls.

onboarding-recommend/chip-editor-open.scenario: The review with the days-per-week chip open on its inline editor: the same numeric cards as the question, an Update program action, and the pinned activation set aside.

onboarding-recommend/result-corrected.scenario: A changed answer rebuilt the program in place: the change statement with Before and Now, an added exercise tagged new, and its day open.

onboarding-recommend/result-avoided.scenario: An exercise the program contained is avoided from the priorities editor: the statement, and the constraint line with Restore.

onboarding-custom/shape.scenario: Two compatible weekly structures to choose from; shown only when more than one fits the answers.

Glyph and word beside a rec.*.label: a redundant mark on flat content, neither a control nor a layer. Up uses the action color, records the improved color, declines ink; hold draws "=" and recover a return arrow, both in ink (owner decision on #295, 2026-10-01), while stalled and new stay word-only. The session outcome "Maintained" draws the same ink "=" as hold (one meaning per glyph, #295 comment 5940349337), so the summary, History session page and Progress Strength rows carry the glyph on every outcome word; the Focus cue draws hold and recover through it too. The landing's three outcomes render it first (R2a-B); Today's prescription rows and tally (R3b) and the Why sheet's headline (R3g) render it; the session summary (R3h) renders it for each lift's outcome word, its record line and the next target. The History session page renders it too (R3j): the lift's outcome word from compareExerciseSession and its record mark. The Program overview renders it too (R3k): the glyph alone beside the next load of a lift whose recommendation adds or backs off load; the row carries the verdict as visually hidden text. Progress renders it too (R3i): the attention rows' mark from the engine's recommendation for each lift whose load changes. The Focus cue draws it too (hold "=", up and down arrows) on every Focus state whose cue moves or holds the load.

The one header band for every sheet: handle, section-title title, optional body-small line and a 44px close reserve, inside the sheet's modal layer. First rendered by the workout sheets (Plan 064 R3d); the note sheet has no close button because its Cancel is the dismiss.

Ledger sets still to do are flat read-only data on one decorative hairline per break, in soft ink with the previous session's matching set as a second line. A logged set is its own row (ledgerline-done) because tapping it reopens the set; the open or corrected row is ledgerline-open (OG-4). The History editor's set rows sit on the same flat ledger, with the three value inputs and the quiet remove in place of read-only values (R3j2).

Moves to another view, detail, or dismisses a layer without committing training state: the whole row opens the exercise. The Program overview renders it first (R3k) as the drawing's three-column form: name with its strategy, sets x range, and the next load with the verdict mark.

The open or corrected ledger row is a selected child on the flat ledger: a well ground and a 2px edge in the quiet selected boundary (ink), no outward shadow. The edge is drawn as the row's border so the rendered-role audit can measure it; it reaches 3:1 on the well and on the page ground in both themes (OG-4).

The row of tabs sits on one decorative hairline; each tab's selected state, not the hairline, carries the required cue. The paper fade drawn while the row overflows is a gradient the rendered-role audit cannot measure, so it is not part of this component. Progress renders it (R3i): one row of five sections above every Progress tab.

Changes the visible evidence panel or scope without committing data. The selected tab carries a 2px indicator in the quiet selected boundary (ink), 3:1 or better on the page ground and the surface in both themes (OG-4); a consumer that needs an id gets its own exact row. Progress renders it (R3i): Overview, Strength, Volume, PRs and Review.

Frequency counts are flat, non-interactive bars of sessions per week and per weekday: one labelled image for assistive technology, bars in ink, a decorative hairline baseline, and an optional planned marker on the required boundary token, never --rule-strong (OG-4). Progress classification (R3j): the bars are a tally of saved sessions, not workflow progress. The per-week bars sit against the program's planned days per week, but that line is a reference mark, not a completion value: no bar reads as a fraction of a goal, weeks not yet reached draw nothing, and the per-weekday bars have no denominator at all. The block total in the image label (done of planned, week n of N) is the only denominator, and it is text. The counts are therefore neither block, week, exercise-set nor task progress, they are not a progress candidate selector, and no data-progress-dimension is declared on them.

The History editor pins Cancel and Save on the same shelf with the dock hidden (R3j2).

contextualVariants.rationale: The creation controls and received-program Start are one recipe, the ink pill with its arrow: the parchment action on the night band, the near-black action on the orange band, the arrow in the action's own ink on parchment (the prototype's orange arrow measured 2.05:1 there) and the orange band's mark on near-black. Owner decision L-1 on PR #295.
The two import controls open the same route without a training-state write; they are underlined text links with no boundary, in the ink of the band they sit on. Owner decision L-1 on PR #295.

The landing's persistent Build control floats with the existing floating elevation and takes the night or orange-band ink that reads against the band beneath it. It is the one floating surface outside the dock, the workout shelf and the sheets, and it is absent on the received-program gate. Owner decision L-1 on PR #295.

The proof's phone plate uses 24px at normal width and 20px at compact width, and each static step crop uses 14px: the Plan 054 device-stage geometry, re-pointed from the retired .firstrun-stage to the final page's plate and crop.
Repeated set changes during an active lift need a compact nearby target; 44px target and focus semantics stay shared.
Programmed set-count edits are slower planning changes; target, focus and disabled semantics stay shared.
The normal destination dock keeps the selected destination visible as a floating glass capsule.
Program edit uses the approved shallow full-width action layer; its meaning stays navigation and the current destination stays selected.
Recommendation is the featured entry action, not a user-selected option.
The first-run gate blocks the app without a card shadow; the final page's bands scroll inside it.
Saved-session completion owns the screen, while its sticky Done bar is a separate persistent action child.
The chosen period changes the denominator; this-week is week and block-to-date is block.

The hero headline and the closing title are the first-run headline variant: above the general display scale, with a distinct wide size (section 8.1). No landing section takes any other off-scale size.
The saved-session summary hero sits between title and display without flattening its completion hierarchy.

The running rest countdown needs responsive Mono numerals in the Focus cue slot: clamp(2rem,10cqi,2.625rem) through --font-size-rest-clock (OG-4, C-02). Selector-exact: no other surface inherits it by visual resemblance.

The workout shelf is a full-width persistent-action surface under Focus with the existing prominent top radius, a shallow top edge and the persistent depth; its fields sit on the well and its pads on the page ground, scoped to the shelf. Selector-exact: no other surface inherits it by visual resemblance (OG-4).

exceptions.rationale: The brand mark keeps its own small paper plate and artwork shadow; it does not elevate surrounding Settings content.
The ground-free mark stands on its paper plate in both appearances, because the hero is the night band in both; the plate is not a selectable or elevated card.

The drain bar is the running rest clock drawn as a transform on a 4px track: it measures time left in this rest, so assigning block, week, exercise-set or task would falsify its denominator. Orange on --rule measures 3.05:1 light and 4.80:1 dark, and against --bg 3.57:1 and 6.33:1 (3:1 required). The bar is not a progress candidate selector.
The illustrated Safari controls are aria-hidden teaching artwork, not live control boundaries.
The licensed illustration keeps its sampled mediaBg paper; its reviewed static fallback remains the same warm plate when metadata is absent.

rootRecipeOwners.sourceOnlyReason: Focus and library glossary popovers have rendered states; the workout overflow menu remains on-demand.

rootRecipeOwners.rationale: The upward shadow belongs to the shared bottom-sheet family, whose modal surface rises from the viewport edge while preserving its separate scrim and keyboard-aware geometry.
Only the exercise row carried during an active reorder gains temporary floating depth; the resting editor rows remain flat.
rootRecipeOwners.sourceOnlyReason: Canonical editor frames show the reorder owner with no row actively dragged.

rootRecipeOwners.rationale: The selected button paints its own lens wherever the dock lens element is not mounted (before boot or without the script). Its inset sheen and restrained edge keep the selected destination legible without outward elevation.

Once the script mounts the dock lens, the single lens element paints the selected pill behind the buttons and travels between them. Its slightly adjusted inset opacity compensates for the different paint layer and keeps the approved selection treatment consistent.
The field halo is a focus-visible facet of the existing field role; the required boundary remains on the field while the translucent ring adds the separate focus cue.
The inset track edge preserves the switch boundary in its unselected state. The selected track uses the existing accent fill and intentionally removes this resting inset.
The small thumb shadow separates the movable switch affordance from its track; it is part of the existing reversible selection control.

One inset keyline reinforces the existing accent boundary on the featured primary card. Entry selections no longer use it: a chosen option takes the quiet ink ring (Q-E, OG-4, --boundary-selected-quiet), so the keyline expresses only the primary role's required boundary and does not alter dimensions or add elevation.
